proposal.title: Vypelpel: an interoperable group messaging library
proposal.summary: Vypelpel builds an interoperable group messaging library for developers of chat applications.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Group messaging libraries differ in how they handle members who leave. Developers of chat applications depend on secure messaging every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build an interoperable group messaging library called Vypelpel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Secure messaging is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/vypelpel/vypelpel, which 183 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on secure messaging for 9 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/vypelpel/vypelpel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 29500.00 EUR for 46 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Group messaging libraries differ in how they handle members who leave. Developers of chat applications depend on secure messaging every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build an interoperable group messaging library called Vypelpel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Secure messaging is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/vypelpel/vypelpel, which 183 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on secure messaging for 9 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the EUPL-1.2 licence in http://forge.test/vypelpel/vypelpel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 29500.00 EUR for 46 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 500.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
